evals.name: api-key-deploy
evals.prompt: Deploy nginx to Akash with API key in $AKASH_API_KEY via CI

assertions.description: Uses the x-api-key header (not Authorization: Bearer for the API key)
Hits /v1/deployments (plural, current)
Wraps request body in { "data": { ... } }
Does NOT use the akash CLI (akash tx/query/keys ...)
Does NOT walk through mTLS certificate generation
Uses POST /v1/leases (batch endpoint that also sends manifest)
Does NOT use Authorization: Bearer with the API key
References the API key via env var, never inline
Does NOT send a deposit field; Console funds deployments automatically

evals.name: ambiguous-deploy
evals.prompt: Want to deploy a node.js+postgres app to Akash. How?

assertions.description: Asks the user which deployment method they want
Lists multiple methods so the user can pick

evals.name: keplr-self-custody
evals.prompt: Have 50 AKT in Keplr, deploy redis to Akash, don't want to give up keys

assertions.description: Mentions a self-custody path (CLI or SDK)

assertions.pattern: (use the console api|via the console api|x-api-key|/v1/deployments)
assertions.description: Does NOT push Console API for this user
Acknowledges the Keplr wallet specifically
Does NOT reference the bogus console-air.akash.network URL (Console Air is self-hosted)

evals.name: stream-logs
evals.prompt: Stream logs from Akash deployment dseq 12345678 via API

assertions.description: Mints JWT via POST /v1/create-jwt-token
Resolves provider hostUri via GET /v1/providers/{address}
Uses WebSocket / WSS for log streaming
Hits provider's /lease/{dseq}/{gseq}/{oseq}/logs endpoint
Does NOT invent a Console-API passthrough for logs
Sends JWT in Authorization: Bearer header on the provider call

evals.name: provider-setup
evals.prompt: Set up Akash provider on 3-node k3s cluster with one 3090 GPU

assertions.description: Covers Kubernetes prerequisites
Mentions installing provider-services daemon
Addresses GPU attribute configuration
Does NOT use uakt as the active denom (legacy/deprecated mentions are OK)

evals.name: validator-setup
evals.prompt: Install Akash validator on mainnet, state sync vs genesis?

assertions.description: Covers full-node installation
Discusses state sync (the user asked)
Mentions becoming a validator on-chain
Mentions validator security (sentry, slashing, key management)

evals.name: method-switch
evals.prompt: Started CLI deployment, want to switch to Console API for accepting bid

assertions.description: Explains the wallet mismatch between CLI self-custody and Console account

assertions.pattern: (just switch|simple swap|yes you can switch to|just use the api now)
assertions.description: Does NOT claim the methods are mid-stream interchangeable
Offers a concrete path forward (finish via CLI, or recreate via API)

evals.name: arm64-sdl
evals.prompt: Write an Akash SDL for my arm64-only image ghcr.io/acme/edge-agent:1.4.2 (port 8080, 1 CPU, 1Gi RAM, 2Gi disk). It must land on ARM nodes.

assertions.description: Requests the architecture via cpu.attributes.arch: arm64
Does NOT use uname/Go spellings or the wrong case as the arch value
Does NOT request the architecture through placement attributes
Keeps the explicit image tag

evals.name: http-proxy-options
evals.prompt: My Akash service streams server-sent events from port 8080, but clients only receive the whole stream once the response ends. Fix it in the SDL.

assertions.description: Disables buffering via http_options.proxy.buffering_disable: true
Nests the block under http_options.proxy
Does NOT use raw nginx directive names as SDL keys
Does NOT use the `buffering` spelling; the SDL field is `buffering_disable`
Never sets buffers_number without buffers_size
Says the proxy block is not honored by providers yet

evals.name: patch-deployment
evals.prompt: My Akash deployment (dseq 1785245500842) was created through the Console API; my key is in $AKASH_API_KEY. I need to roll the `api` service to image ghcr.io/acme/api:2.4.1 and set its LOG_LEVEL env var to debug, without touching anything else in the deployment. Give me the curl.

assertions.description: Updates with PATCH /v1/deployments/{dseq}
Does NOT send the deprecated full-SDL PUT
Patches the api service by name under data.services
Sets the new image on the service
Patches env as a name-to-value map, not a list of KEY=VALUE strings

evals.name: accept-bid-no-manifest
evals.prompt: I created an Akash deployment with POST /v1/deployments (dseq 1785245500842) and bids have arrived. My API key is in $AKASH_API_KEY. Write the bash that picks the cheapest bid and creates the lease.

assertions.description: Creates the lease with POST /v1/leases
Does NOT send the deprecated manifest field; Console sends the manifest it stored at create
Copies the provider from bid.id
Picks the cheapest bid by price.amount

evals.name: sealed-secrets
evals.prompt: I'm deploying a Postgres-backed app to Akash from a Node.js script using the Console API (key in AKASH_API_KEY). The DB password and a Stripe secret key must not be readable back from the Console API after the deploy. How do I pass them? Show the code.

assertions.description: References each secret in the SDL as ac-secret://NAME
Sends the values in sealedSecrets
Fetches the sealing key from GET /v1/sdl-secrets-context
Seals with RSA-OAEP-256
Encrypts the content with A256GCM

evals.name: list-deployments-paginated
evals.prompt: Using the Akash Console API with $AKASH_API_KEY, write a bash script that prints the dseq and name of every deployment I own, including closed ones.

assertions.description: Pages on data.pagination.hasMore
Asks for closed deployments explicitly; the list defaults to active ones
Does NOT ask for more than 100 deployments per page
Reads data.deployments, not a bare array

evals.name: jwt-full-access
evals.prompt: From my CI job (Akash Console API key in $AKASH_API_KEY), I want a single provider JWT that allows every action on every lease I own: logs, shell, events, status, everything. What's the create-jwt-token request?

assertions.description: Mints the JWT with POST /v1/create-jwt-token
Uses leases { access: full } with nothing else
Does NOT attach a scope list to access: full, which the JWT schema rejects

evals.name: account-balance
evals.prompt: Quick one: with my Akash Console API key in $AKASH_API_KEY, how do I check from a script how much credit I have left and how much is held by my running deployments?

assertions.description: Reads GET /v1/balances
Does NOT require the wallet address; the API key identifies the account
Calls the held part escrow

evals.name: tee-attestation
evals.prompt: I have a confidential compute (TEE) deployment on Akash that I created via the Console API (dseq 1785245500842, gseq 1, oseq 1; API key in $AKASH_API_KEY). How do I fetch and verify its attestation evidence from a script?

assertions.description: Fetches the evidence from the provider's /lease/{dseq}/{gseq}/{oseq}/attestation/quote
Mints a JWT carrying the attestation scope
Validates the evidence with POST /v1/confidential-compute/attestation/validate
Sends a fresh nonce

evals.name: change-resources
evals.prompt: My Akash deployment 1785245500842 (created via the Console API, key in $AKASH_API_KEY) needs 4 CPUs instead of 2 and 8Gi of memory instead of 4Gi. How do I update it in place?

assertions.description: Does NOT send a full-SDL PUT, which is deprecated and refuses resource changes
Explains a resource change needs a new deployment

assertions.pattern: (?i)(422|deployment_resources_changed|can(no|')t (be )?change|cannot be changed|fixed at create|not possible in place|can't be updated in place|cannot be updated in place)
assertions.description: Says compute resources cannot change in place

evals.name: akt-ci-console-deploy
evals.prompt: Our GitHub Actions runner has akt 1.0.0 (the Akash CLI) installed, and the Console API key is in a repository secret. Write the workflow steps that deploy `app.yaml` to Akash through Console with no prompts, take whichever bid is cheapest, and pass the deployment's dseq to later steps.

assertions.description: Deploys with `akt deploy app.yaml`
Passes the key through AKT_CONSOLE_API_KEY
Creates a console context first; a fresh runner has none and akt has no wizard without a terminal
Picks the bid non-interactively with --bid-select cheapest
Skips confirmation prompts with --yes
Requests JSON or JSONL output to parse
Extracts the dseq from the machine output
Passes no deposit, which akt 1.0 rejects on the console rail
Stays on akt instead of hand-writing Console API calls

evals.name: akt-0-1-console-deposit
evals.prompt: I installed akt with Homebrew (`akt version` prints 0.1.2) and set up a Console context. Running `akt deploy svc.yaml --bid-select cheapest --yes` stops with: deposit "auto": console-api deployments require an explicit USD amount of at least $0.50. I thought Console funds deployments on its own now. What should I run?

assertions.description: On 0.1.x, passes a USD deposit of at least $0.50
Says akt 1.0 drops the deposit requirement
Explains Console ignores the amount and funds the deployment itself

evals.name: akt-console-logs-shell
evals.prompt: Using akt with my Console context, get the last 200 log lines from the `worker` service of deployment 4419827, then check whether /data/cache exists inside that container.

assertions.description: Uses `akt console logs <dseq> <service>`
Limits output with --tail 200
Runs a one-off command with `akt console shell <dseq> <service> -- <cmd>`
Does not run chain-rail or provider-services commands for a Console deployment

evals.name: akt-update-image
evals.prompt: Deployment 7712004 was created with `akt deploy stack.yaml` on a Console context. I want to bump the api service from ghcr.io/acme/api:5.1.0 to ghcr.io/acme/api:5.2.0. What's the akt way to do it?

assertions.description: Runs `akt update <sdl> <dseq>` with the SDL first
Does not put the dseq before the SDL
Validates the edited SDL before updating
Stays on akt instead of switching to raw HTTP

evals.name: akt-mcp-claude-code
evals.prompt: I'd like Claude Code to use akt as an MCP server so it can read my Akash deployments. How do I hook it up, and will it be able to close deployments?

assertions.description: Launches the server with `akt mcp`
Registers it with `claude mcp add`
Names --enable-writes as the switch for close and other writes
Says the server is read-only by default

evals.name: akt-terminal-postgres
evals.prompt: akt is on my PATH and my Console context works. From this terminal, spin up a throwaway Postgres 16 on Akash for testing.

assertions.description: Deploys with `akt deploy`
Chooses the bid with --bid-select instead of an interactive picker an agent cannot answer
Validates the SDL before deploying
Pins postgres:16 rather than latest
Prices the SDL in uact
Stays on akt instead of hand-writing Console API calls
Does not run provider-services commands
